AD_COLUMN.NAME: Default Value
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The first non-null value in a set of values. It is used as a default value for a field when creating a record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Length
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An indication of the column length as defined in the database.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Length indicates the length of a column as defined in the database.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Key Column

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The key column must also be display sequence 0 in the field definition and may be hidden.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Link to Parent Column
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: This column is a link to the parent table (e.g. header from lines) - incl. Association key columns
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Parent checkbox indicates if this column is a link to the parent table.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Mandatory checkbox indicates if the field is required for a record to be save to the database.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Used for Record ID
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The document number will be used as the record key
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Used for Record ID checkbox indicates if the document id will be used as the key to the record

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Data Access Level
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Credit

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.HELP: A more descriptive identifier (that does need to be unique) of a record/document that is used as a default search option along with the search key (that is unique and mostly shorter). It is up to 60 characters in length.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Description
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A space to write additional related information.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: A description is limited to 255 characters.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: GAAP
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The GAAP identifies the account principles that this accounting schema will adhere to.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Accrual
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates if Accrual or Cash Based accounting will be used
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Accrual checkbox indicates if this accounting schema will use accrual based account or cash based accounting. The Accrual method recognizes revenue when the product or service is delivered. Cash based method recognizes income when then payment is received.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Costing Method
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates how costs will be calculated
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Indicates how costs will be calculated (Standard, Average) for valuation and accounting purposes.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Currency
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An accepted medium of monetary exchange that may vary across countries.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Indicates the currency to be used when processing this document.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Automatic Period Control
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: If selected, the periods are automatically opened and closed
AD_COLUMN.HELP: In the Automatic Period Control, periods are opened and closed based on the current date. If the Manual alternative is activated, you have to open and close periods explicitly.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Period
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A specified time period.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Period indicates an exclusive range of dates for a calendar.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: History Days
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Number of days to be able to post in the past (based on system date)
AD_COLUMN.HELP: If Automatic Period Control is enabled, the current period is calculated based on the system date and you can always post to all days in the current period. History Days enable to post to previous periods. E.g. today is May 15th and History Days is set to 30, you can post back to April 15th

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Future Days
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Number of days to be able to post to a future date (based on system date)
AD_COLUMN.HELP: If Automatic Period Control is enabled, the current period is calculated based on the system date and you can always post to all days in the current period. Future Days enable to post to future periods. E.g. today is Apr 15th and Future Days is set to 30, you can post up to May 15th

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Customer Balance indicates the total amount of open or unpaid invoices for this Business Partner.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Acquisition Cost

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Acquisition Cost identifies the cost associated with making this prospect a customer.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Expected Lifetime Revenue
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Total Revenue expected
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Potential Life Time Value is the anticipated revenue to be generated by this Business Partner.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Payment Terms

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Lifetime Revenue to Date

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Actual Life Time Value is the recorded revenue to be generated by this Business Partner.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Share

AD_COLUMN.HELP: An organization is a unit of your client or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Fixed Due Date
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Payment is due on a fixed date
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Fixed Due Date checkbox indicates if invoices using this payment term will be due on a fixed day of the month.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Maturity Date 1
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The day of the month that invoices are due. 3 maturity dates can be defined.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Fix Month Day indicates the day of the month that invoices are due. This field is displayed only when the fixed due date checkbox is selected. 3 different fix month days can be defined.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Offset Month Due
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Number of months (0=same, 1=following)
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Offset Month Due indicates the number of months from the current month to indicate an invoice is due. A 0 indicates the same month, a 1 the following month.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: SO Sub Type
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Sales Order Sub Type
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
The SO Sub Type indicates the type of sales order this document refers to. This field only appears when the Document Base Type is Sales Order. The selection made here will determine which documents will be generated when an order is processed and which documents must be generated manually or in batches.
The following outlines this process.
SO Sub Type of Standard Order will generate just the Order document when the order is processed.
The Delivery Note, Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Warehouse Order will generate the Order and Delivery Note.
The Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Invoice Cut-Off Day
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Last day for including shipments
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Invoice Day Cut Off indicates the last day for shipments to be included in the current invoice schedule. For example, if the invoice schedule is defined for the first day of the month, the cut off day may be the 25th of the month. An shipment on the 24th of May would be included in the invoices sent on June 1st but a shipment on the 26th would be included in the invoices sent on July 1st.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Default Value
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The first non-null value in a set of values. It is used as a default value for a field when creating a record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Value Format

AD_COLUMN.HELP: Value Format is the format the value will be displayed with.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Price List

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.HELP: A Business Partner is anyone with whom you transact. This can include a customer, vendor, employee or any combination of these.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Partner Address
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The location of the selected business partner.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Partner address indicates the location of a Business Partner

AD_COLUMN.NAME: User/Contact
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An acquaintance to reach for information related to the business partner.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The User identifies a unique user in the system. This could be an internal user or a business partner contact

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Business Partner Category
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A classification of business partners based on defined similarities.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: A way of grouping business partners together for classification and reporting purposes. Provides a method of defining certain defaults to be used when opening new business partners.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Order Reference
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A reference or document order number as listed in business partner application.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: This can be used to input a reference for this specific transaction. For example, a Purchase Order number can be input on a Sales Order for easier reference.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Order Date
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The time listed on the order.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Indicates the Date an item was ordered.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Currency
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An accepted medium of monetary exchange that may vary across countries.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Indicates the currency to be used when processing this document.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Form of Payment
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The method used for payment of this transaction.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Form of Payment indicates the method of payment used for this transaction (eg. cash, wire transfer, etc.)

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Payment Terms
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The setup and timing defined to complete a specified payment.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Payment Terms identify the method and timing of payment for this transaction.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Price List
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A catalog of selected items with prices defined generally or for a specific partner.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Price Lists are used to determine the pricing, margin and cost of items purchased or sold.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Sales Campaign
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An advertising effort aimed at increasing sales.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Campaign defines a unique marketing program. Projects can be associated with a pre defined Marketing Campaign. You can then report based on a specific Campaign.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Project
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Identifier of a project defined within the Project & Service Management module.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Identifier of a project defined within the Project & Service Management module.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Activity
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A distinct activity defined and used in activity based management.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Activities indicate tasks that are performed and used to utilize Activity based Costing

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Charge
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A cost or expense incurred during business activity.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Charge indicates a type of Charge (Handling, Shipping, Restocking)

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Charge Amount
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The amount of a cost or expense incurred during business activity.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Charge Amount indicates the amount for an additional charge.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Summed Line Amount
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The final sum of all line totals made to a specified document or transaction (not including taxes).
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Total amount displays the total of all lines in document currency

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Grand Total Amount
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The final monetary amount (including taxes) charge listed in a document.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Grand Total displays the total amount including Tax and Freight in document currency

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Multiplier
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Number of times needed to run this sequence in order to satisfy the complete process plan.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Discount indicates the discount applied or taken as a percentage.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Margin indicates the margin for this product as a percentage of the limit price and selling price.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The final amount of a specified line, based only on quantities and prices.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Line Discount
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Line Discount Amount
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Indicates the discount for this line as an amount.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Default Logic 2
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Default value hierarchy, separated by ;
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Data Access Level
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.HELP: Identifies the category which this product belongs to. Product categories are used for pricing.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Tax Category
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A classification of tax options based on similar characteristics or attributes.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Tax Category provides a method of grouping similar taxes. For example, Sales Tax or Value Added Tax.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Name
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A non-unique identifier for a record/document often used as a search tool.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: A more descriptive identifier (that does need to be unique) of a record/document that is used as a default search option along with the search key (that is unique and mostly shorter). It is up to 60 characters in length.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Description
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A space to write additional related information.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: A description is limited to 255 characters.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Sequence Tab
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The Tab determines the Order
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Tab determines the Order.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Included Column
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Column determining if a Table Column is included in Ordering
AD_COLUMN.HELP: If a Included Column is defined, it decides, if a column is active in the ordering - otherwise it is determined that the Order Column has a value of one or greater

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Order Column
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Column determining the order
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Integer Column of the table determining the order (display, sort, ..). If defined, the Order By replaces the default Order By clause. It should be fully qualified (i.e. "tablename.columnname").

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Invoice Price
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The price at which something may be invoiced, shown in the currency of the invoiced business partner.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Unit Price in the currency of the business partner! If it is 0, the standard price of the sales price list of the business partner (customer) is used.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: City
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A populated defined area located within a larger area such as a state, province, or country.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: City in a country

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Currency
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An accepted medium of monetary exchange that may vary across countries.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Indicates the currency to be used when processing this document.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Language
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A method of communication being used.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Language identifies the language to use for display

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Postal Code field identifies the postal code for this entity's address.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A populated defined area located within a larger area such as a state, province, or country.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Region

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Abbreviation
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Location code - UN/LOCODE

UN/Locode is a combination of a 2-character country code and a 3-character location code, e.g. BEANR is known as the city of Antwerp (ANR) which is located in Belgium (BE).

See: http://www.unece.org/cefact/locode/service/main.htm

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Area Code

AD_COLUMN.HELP:
This column contains the geographical coordinates (latitude/longitude) of the location.

0000N 00000W 0000S 00000E

Please note, that the base language is always English.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: User Name (ID) in the Mail System
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The user name in the mail system is usually the string before the @ of your email address. Required if the mail server requires authentification to send emails.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Invoice Grouping
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
For scheduled invoicing, break into different invoices if the related values are different. The value is used as a binary code with 15 digits: 1.-Order organization (AD_Org_ID) 2.-Order (C_Order_ID) 3.-Shipment (M_InOut_ID) 4.-Invoice location (BillTo_ID) 5.-Ship location (C_BPartner_Location_ID) 6.-Sales representative (SalesRep_ID) 7.-Payment rule (PaymentRule) 8.-Payment term (C_PaymentTerm_ID) 9.-Currency (C_Currency_ID) 10.-Campaign (C_Campaign_ID) 11.-Project (C_Project_ID) 12.-Activity (C_Activity_ID) 13.-Transaction organization (AD_OrgTrx_ID) 14.-User defined 1 (User1) 15.-User defined 2 (User2)
For example, if you want to create different invoices for each ship location for a customer, use the value "By ship location" (000010000000000)

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Processed

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Processed checkbox indicates that a document has been processed.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Name
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A non-unique identifier for a record/document often used as a search tool.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: A more descriptive identifier (that does need to be unique) of a record/document that is used as a default search option along with the search key (that is unique and mostly shorter). It is up to 60 characters in length.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: A description is limited to 255 characters.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The sequence relates the operations with the process plan.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: IBAN
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: International standard for identifying bank accounts across national borders
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Code that identifies uniquely one bank account, no matter the country it belongs to. It consists of a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, followed by two check digits, and up to thirty alphanumeric characters for the domestic bank account number, called the BBAN (Basic Bank Account Number). It is up to each country's national banking community to decide on the length of the BBAN for accounts in that country, but its length must be fixed for any given country.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Country
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A state or a nation.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Country defines a Country. Each Country must be defined before it can be used in any document.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: IBAN Length
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The length of the IBAN code of a bank account is variable, depending on the country.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Then International Bank Account Number structure do not stablish a specific length: it depends on the country. This field will define the length of the IBAN codes for that country.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: IBAN Code
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Country Code asigned to a country in the IBAN structure.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Then International Bank Account Number structure stablish that the first two digits will belong to the country. This country code is the one associated to a country of the application in this field.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Generic Account

A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Secondarywhereclause
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: This is a secondary SQL where clause used by dbsourcemanager to filter data inside a table.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: This is a secondary SQL where clause used by dbsourcemanager to filter data inside a table. This secondary whereclause needs to be written in SQL, and only applies for the dataset AD. When export.database is executed, this whereclause will be applied for the data inside the table, and only the records complying with it will be exported. The rest of the records (the ones which do not comply with the whereclause) will be ignored both in export.database and update.database. The main purpose of this whereclause is to select which of the records in a particular table are part of sourcedata, and which ones are part of client data.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates whether the report is "Point in time" (needs to calculate an opening balance if it does not exist) or a "Periodic" report (in this case that calculation is not needed)
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Indicates whether the report is a "Point in Time" or a "Periodic" report.
A Point in Time report is obtained as of a given date, taking into account the whole historical financial movements; an example of point in time report is the Balance Sheet.
A periodic report is executed for a date range and it does not carry forward the balance of accounting movements previous to the range; an example of periodic report is the Income Statement.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.DEFAULTVALUE: @SQL=SELECT FIN_Payment_Priority_ID FROM FIN_Payment_Priority WHERE AD_ISORGINCLUDED( (CASE WHEN @#AD_Org_ID@='0' THEN (SELECT ad_org_id FROM ad_org WHERE name = ( SELECT min(o.name) FROM ad_org o join ad_orgtype ot on (o.ad_orgtype_id=ot.ad_orgtype_id) join ad_role_orgaccess ra on (o.ad_org_id=ra.ad_org_id) join ad_role r on (ra.ad_role_id = r.ad_role_id) WHERE ot.istransactionsallowed = 'Y' and r.ad_role_id=@AD_Role_ID@)) ELSE @#AD_Org_ID@ END), AD_Org_ID, @#AD_Client_ID@) <> -1 AND Isdefault = 'Y' ORDER BY Priority

AD_COLUMN.HELP: An AD_Table record has a mandatory relation to a package (the AD_Package). Choose a sensible package fitting to the functional area to which the table applies (so not the Core package). If no such package exist then create a new one. The relation to the module is maintained through the AD_Package, so an AD_Table has an AD_Package which belongs to a module. When developing for a module then first a package needs to be defined in AD_Package, linked to the module. Then the records in AD_Table (for that module) can be linked to that package.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Dependency Enforcement
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Dependency enforcement defines which are the versions of the dependent module that are compatible with the parent one.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Dependency enforcement defines which are the versions of the dependent module that are compatible with the parent one.
The values it can contain are:
*Major Version (default). The compatible versions are all the minor version within the same major version. If "Last Version" is defined being a different major version than "From Version", "Last Version" defines the highest compatible minor version; if "Last Version" is in the same major version than "From Version" this value is not taken into account. It is the default value. *Minor Version. Defines a strict dependency to the exact minor version. In case no "Last Version" is set, "From Version" is the only compatible version. Other case the compatible versions are all between "From" and "Last Version" values. *None. "From Version" is the only field taken into account, there is no restriction on different major versions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: User Editable Enforcement
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Defines whether the enforcement can be overwritten by user
AD_COLUMN.HELP: When a dependency/inclusion is "User Editable Enforcement", the enforcement defined for that dependency can be overwritten at instance level.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Instance Enforcement
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Instance specific dependency enforcement
AD_COLUMN.HELP: In case the dependency is set as "User Editable", this value overwrites the Instance Enforcement one.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.
